title: Your first tri starts here
intro: You don't need to be fast, fit or own a fancy bike. Here's what a triathlon is, what to expect, and how to get started with us.

blocks.title: What is a triathlon?
paragraphs: A triathlon is three sports back to back: swim, then bike, then run. The clock keeps running through the two transitions, where you switch gear in a designated area.
Races come in many lengths, and most people start with a sprint. Plenty of first-timers finish a sprint after a couple of months of steady training.

blocks.title: Pick a distance
blocks.note: Distances vary a little from race to race. Always check the race's own course info.

blocks.title: What you actually need
blocks.intro: Start with what you have. You can upgrade later, if you ever want to.

groups.title: Swim
items: Goggles that fit and don't leak
Swim cap (the race usually provides one)
Wetsuit only if the race is cold-water and you want one

groups.title: Bike
items: Any road, hybrid or mountain bike in good working order
A helmet that fits (required in races)
Spare tube, pump or CO2 and tire levers

groups.title: Run
items: Race belt for your bib number (or safety pins)

items.title: Set up
items.text: Arrive early, rack your bike, and lay out your gear in the transition area. Walk through the swim exit, bike out and run out so you know the way.

items.title: Swim
items.text: Start easy and find your rhythm. It's fine to float, flip to your back or hold a buoy for a moment. Nobody minds.

items.title: Bike and run
items.text: Helmet on before you touch the bike. Drink on the bike, ease into the run, and finish with a smile. Your legs will feel odd for the first few minutes, and that's normal.

items.title: "I'm not a strong swimmer."
items.text: Plenty of people aren't. Pool swims with a lane to yourself are a great place to build comfort before open water.

items.title: "I don't have a tri bike."
items.text: You don't need one. Any bike in good shape will get you through a first race.

items.title: "What if I'm last?"
items.text: Someone always has the best seat in the house. Finishing a triathlon at all puts you ahead of everyone on the couch.

items.q: How long should I train before a first sprint?
items.a: Many beginners train for 8 to 12 weeks with 3 to 4 sessions a week. If you can already swim a few lengths, ride an hour and jog 20 to 30 minutes, you are most of the way there.
A bike ride followed straight away by a short run, so your legs get used to the switch.

items.q: Can I do group sessions as a beginner?
items.a: Yes. Come to a session, go at your own pace, and introduce yourself. Check the schedule for the next one.

blocks.title: Ready to try one?
blocks.text: Pick a session from the schedule and come say hi.
